analysis.summary: Krishana Phoschem reported Q1 FY27 quarterly revenue from operations of ₹ 532 crore, EBITDA of ₹ 89 crore, and profit after tax of ₹ 47 crore. During the quarter, the company achieved fertilizer production of 89,747 metric tonnes, with capacity utilization standing at 43% for its NPK-DAP unit and 121% for its SSP unit. Management stated that the quarter faced operational challenges due to global supply-side disruptions and elevated raw material prices, but expects improved performance across the remaining quarters of FY27 as raw material availability normalizes. Krishana Phoschem Limited commenced FY27 on a resilient note, with quarterly revenue growing 34.58% YoY to ₹532.3 crore and quarterly Profit After Tax increasing 53.88% YoY to ₹47.06 crore. The company's expanded capacities at Meghnagar for NPK/DAP and Sulphuric Acid are now contributing progressively to its performance.

guidance.claim: Management expects to achieve an additional 30% to 35% turnover over last year as production smoothens over remaining quarters.
guidance.quote: We are hoping that over the remaining quarters, we will be able to smoothen our production, and we will be able to achieve an additional 30%–35% turnover over last year.

guidance.claim: The company expects to achieve a quarterly turnover of more than ₹500 crore over the remaining three quarters of FY27.
guidance.quote: We expect to achieve a quarterly turnover of more than ₹500 crore over the remaining three quarters of FY27, supported by improved capacity utilization and production.

guidance.claim: Utilization of the newly commissioned NPK capacity is expected to steadily ramp up over coming quarters.
guidance.quote: The NPK capacity commission during the previous quarter is expected to witness a steady ramp-up in utilization over the coming quarters.

guidance.claim: Management is confident of building on its operational and financial momentum through the remainder of FY27.
guidance.quote: We are confident of building on this momentum through the remainder of FY27, as we continue strengthening India's agri-future for our farmers, partners, & shareholders

guidance.claim: The company expects to deliver over 40% growth across key parameters during the current fiscal year.
guidance.quote: Accordingly, we expect to deliver growth of over 40% across key parameters during the current year.

guidance.claim: Management expects top line to increase by around Rs. 500 crore from expanded capacity in FY27.
guidance.quote: So, you expect an increase of around Rs. 500 crore more, Rs. 2,900 to Rs. 3,000.

guidance.claim: The company anticipates overall revenue growth of 35%-40% in FY27 from manufacturing and trading.
guidance.quote: So overall, we hope 35%-40% revenue growth in FY27.

guidance.claim: Krishana Phoschem expects to import around 150,000 metric tons of material generating approximately Rs. 1,000 crore revenue in FY27.
guidance.quote: For FY27, based on market demand, we expect to import around 150,000 metric tons of material, which would translate into approximately Rs.1,000 crore of revenue.

demand_outlook.claim: Cumulative rainfall by end of June was nearly 40% below normal, causing national Kharif sowing to decline 22.7% year-on-year to 182.7 lakh hectares.
demand_outlook.quote: By the end of June, cumulative rainfall was nearly 40% below normal, resulting in national Kharif sowing declining by 22.7% year-on-year to 182.7 lakh hectares, compared to 236.5 lakh hectares during the corresponding period last year.

demand_outlook.claim: Early July rainfall revival resulted in a rapid recovery in sowing progress and accelerated fertilizer offtake.
demand_outlook.quote: However, rainfall improved materially during early July, resulting in a rapid recovery in sowing progress, improved farmer sentiment, and accelerated fertilizer offtake across several key markets for the remainder of the Kharif season.

demand_outlook.claim: Improving monsoon conditions, higher MSPs, and NBS subsidy framework support are expected to sustain fertilizer demand in FY27.
demand_outlook.quote: Improving in monsoon conditions, higher MSP and continued government support through the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) framework are expected to support the fertilizer demand during the remainder of FY27.

demand_outlook.claim: Improving monsoon conditions, higher MSP, and continued government backing through the NBS framework are creating a favorable operating environment.
demand_outlook.quote: Improving monsoon conditions, higher MSP & continued government backing through the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) framework are creating a favourable operating environment.

demand_outlook.claim: The Kharif season demand environment appears constructive for the industry due to comfortable domestic stock levels and a favorable monsoon forecast.
demand_outlook.quote: With comfortable domestic stock levels & a favourable monsoon forecast, the Kharif season demand environment appears constructive for the industry.

demand_outlook.claim: A stable agricultural environment and favorable monsoon outlook provide a constructive demand outlook for fertilizers.
demand_outlook.quote: On one hand, a stable agricultural environment supported by a favorable monsoon outlook provides a constructive demand outlook.

demand_outlook.claim: Domestic manufacturers are expected to remain relatively insulated from demand softening as imports absorb initial impacts.
demand_outlook.quote: Even hypothetically, if demand were to soften, it is important to note that nearly 40% of phosphatic fertilizers are imported. Therefore, any impact would first be absorbed by imports, and domestic manufacturers would remain relatively insulated.

demand_outlook.claim: Demand for NPK variants is rising in India, leading the company to operate plants purely on one high-demand variant.
demand_outlook.quote: Obviously, what happened in the last earning call also, I explained that the demand for different variants of NPK is rising in India. We have been producing one variant at 20-20-0-13 and even the demand of this product, we have not been able to meet adequately.

capex_expansion.claim: Krishana Phoschem is currently evaluating certain capacity expansion opportunities.
capex_expansion.quote: We are currently evaluating certain capacity expansion opportunities.

capex_expansion.claim: The company expanded its product portfolio by introducing complex fertilizer variants including 12:32:16, 16:20:0:13, 15:15:15, 8:21:21, and 9:24:24.
capex_expansion.quote: As part of this initiative, we introduced 12:32:16, 16:20:0:13, 15:15:15, 8:21:21, & 9:24:24.

capex_expansion.claim: The company's expanded capacities at Meghnagar, including NPK/DAP at 165,000 MTPA and Sulphuric Acid at 99,000 MTPA, are now contributing progressively to performance.
capex_expansion.quote: Our expanded capacities at Meghnagar — NPK/DAP at 165,000 MTPA and Sulphuric Acid at 99,000 MTPA — are now contributing progressively to our performance.

capex_expansion.claim: The company enhanced its NPK/DAP capacity by 50% to 495,000 MTPA, taking total phosphatic fertilizer capacity to 615,000 MTPA.
capex_expansion.quote: NPK/DAP capacity enhanced by 50% to 495,000 MTPA and existing SSP capacity at 120,000 MTPA, taking total phosphatic fertilizer capacity to 615,000 MTPA

capex_expansion.claim: Krishana Phoschem expanded its backward integration by strengthening sulphuric acid capacity to 99,000 MTPA.
capex_expansion.quote: Backward integration strengthened with sulphuric acid capacity of 99,000 MTPA

capex_expansion.claim: The company signed a 10-year Green Ammonia Sale Agreement for 70,000 MTPA under National Green Hydrogen Mission.
capex_expansion.quote: As part of our long-term sustainability strategy, Krishana Phoschem has entered into a 10-year Green Ammonia Sale Agreement (GASA) under India’s National Green Hydrogen Mission for 70,000 MTPA.

capex_expansion.claim: Management currently has no additional capex or expansion plans planned beyond completed projects.
capex_expansion.quote: No, so far, we have not planned anything. Whatever we have, it has been implemented.

margins_costs.claim: Quarterly EBITDA reached ₹ 89 crore, registering 36% year-on-year growth.
margins_costs.quote: Quarterly EBITDA stood at ₹ 89 crore, reflecting a 36% year-on-year growth, supported by disciplined cost management, despite volatility in raw material prices.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA margin stands at approximately 7% to 8% for trading and around 16% for manufacturing.
margins_costs.quote: The EBITDA margin is approximately 7%–8% for trading and around 16% for manufacturing.

margins_costs.claim: The company has passed on approximately 25% to 30% of input cost increases through higher subsidies and revised MRPs.
margins_costs.quote: Overall, we have been able to pass on ~ 25%–30% of the increase in input costs.

margins_costs.claim: Depreciation increased to ₹13 crore and finance costs rose to ₹20 crore following capacity commissioning.
margins_costs.quote: Depreciation increased from around ₹8.7 crore to ₹13 crore, while finance costs increased from around ₹13 crore to ₹20 crore.

margins_costs.claim: Sulphur prices rose from ₹65,000–₹70,000 per tonne in April to nearly ₹1 lakh per tonne in June and July.
margins_costs.quote: Sulphur prices have risen from around ₹65,000–₹70,000 per tonne in April to almost ₹1 lakh per tonne in June and July.

margins_costs.claim: Quarterly Profit After Tax grew 53.88% YoY to ₹47.06 crore, reflecting improved operating efficiency and disciplined cost control.
margins_costs.quote: Quaterly Profit After Tax grew 53.88% YoY to ₹47.06 crore, reflecting improved operating efficiency and disciplined cost control.

margins_costs.claim: Profitability is expected to come down slightly during FY27 as the company absorbs part of the sharp input cost increase.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, of course, we will absorb to some extent and as a result, our profitability is expected to come down slightly during the current year FY27.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA per ton on the manufacturing side stood in the range of Rs. 5,500 per ton in FY26.
margins_costs.quote: It was in the range of Rs.5,500 per ton.

margins_costs.claim: Overall EBITDA margin moderated from 13.54% in FY25 to 12.34% in FY26.
margins_costs.quote: Our overall EBITDA margin, which was 13.54% has come down to 12.34%.

margins_costs.claim: Trading operations carry an EBITDA margin of 5% to 6%.
margins_costs.quote: EBITDA margin is 5% to 6% in in trading business.

orders_capacity.claim: Total fertilizer production reached 89,747 metric tonnes during Q1 FY27.
orders_capacity.quote: Achieved fertilizer production of 89,747 metric tonnes, showcasing our consistent operational efficiency.

orders_capacity.claim: Capacity utilization was 43% for the NPK-DAP unit and 121% for the SSP unit in Q1 FY27.
orders_capacity.quote: 43% capacity utilization of NPK-DAP unit and 121% capacity utilization of SSP unit, which was beyond the core.

orders_capacity.claim: The company added 165,000 MT of NPK-DAP capacity to its existing 330,000 MT, bringing total capacity to 495,000 MT.
orders_capacity.quote: Our existing NPK-DAP capacity is 330,000 MT, and we have added another 165,000 MT, taking the total capacity to 495,000 MT.

orders_capacity.claim: The company has an installed capacity of 6.15 Lakh MTPA.
Krishana Phoschem achieved total fertilizer production of 397,263 MT in FY26.
orders_capacity.quote: Achieved total production of 397,263 MT, supported by High demand across markets

orders_capacity.claim: NPK/DAP and SSP plants operated above rated capacity during FY26.
orders_capacity.quote: Record high utilization levels in NPK/DAP and SSP plants operating above rated capacity, highlighting strong market acceptance and efficient asset utilization

orders_capacity.claim: Manufacturing volumes reached around 383,000 MT while trading volumes were approximately 93,000 MT in FY26.
orders_capacity.quote: Trading volumes were approximately 93,000 metric tons, while manufacturing volumes were around 383,000 metric tons.

orders_capacity.claim: Rock phosphate beneficiation capacity is around 200,000 tons with current utilization between 50% and 75%.
orders_capacity.quote: The beneficiation capacity is around 200,000 tons, and current utilization is in the range of 50% to 75%.

capital_allocation.claim: The company executed a 5-for-1 stock split, subdividing equity share face value from ₹10 to ₹2.
capital_allocation.quote: Recently, the company successfully executed a 5-for-1 stock split, subdividing the face value of our equity shares from ₹ 10 per share to ₹ 2 per share.

capital_allocation.claim: Receivables collection during Q1 was more than ₹700 crore.
capital_allocation.quote: Collection is more than Rs. 700 crore.

capital_allocation.claim: The company's strategic blueprint includes disciplined capital allocation as one of its five core pillars.
capital_allocation.quote: Our strategic blueprint rests on five core pillars: backward integration, capacity expansion, product diversification, disciplined capital allocation and deep farmer connect.

capital_allocation.claim: The company remains focused on disciplined execution and long-term value creation.
capital_allocation.quote: With a fundamentally stronger & more efficient asset base now in place, we remain focused on disciplined execution & long-term value creation.

capital_allocation.claim: Capacity expansion was funded through a mix of internal accruals and term loans.
capital_allocation.quote: This expansion has been funded through a prudent mix of internal accruals and term loans, reflecting disciplined capital allocation.

capital_allocation.claim: CRISIL upgraded the company's credit rating to A+ (Stable).
capital_allocation.quote: We are also pleased to highlight that our credit rating has been upgraded by CRISIL to A+ (Stable), reflecting improved financial strength and business fundamentals

capital_allocation.claim: Effective interest cost across borrowing facilities ranges between 6% and 7.5%.
capital_allocation.quote: Overall, the effective interest cost is in the range of 6% to 7.5%.

risks_headwinds.claim: Q1 FY27 faced operational headwinds from global supply-side disruptions, elevated raw material prices, and geopolitical uncertainties.
risks_headwinds.quote: The 1st Quarter witnessed a challenging operating environment for the phosphatic supplier industry, primarily driven by global supply-side disruptions, elevated raw material prices, and geopolitical uncertainties.

risks_headwinds.claim: Geopolitical tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz caused freight cost increases, vessel delays, and higher procurement costs.
risks_headwinds.quote: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia, particularly surrounding critical shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz, introduced considerable uncertainty across global industry, global fertilizer supply chains during the quarter.

risks_headwinds.claim: Raw material availability was the primary operational challenge during the first quarter.
risks_headwinds.quote: The primary challenge during the first quarter was the availability of raw materials.

risks_headwinds.claim: Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially include market conditions, regulatory changes, competitive pressures, and technological advancements.
risks_headwinds.quote: Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially include market conditions, regulatory changes, competitive pressures, and technological advancements.

risks_headwinds.claim: Global input prices for ammonia and sulphur increased towards late Q4 FY26 due to supply constraints and higher freight costs.
risks_headwinds.quote: However, from mid-February onwards, global market witnessed firming trends driven by supply-side constraints, tightness in gas-linked production, higher logistic and freight costs.

risks_headwinds.claim: First-quarter operating margins face pressure from higher raw material costs before MRP revisions stabilize performance.
risks_headwinds.quote: While there may be some margin pressure in the first quarter, we expect margins to stabilize in the later part of the year as cost increases are passed on.
